paper_title: Breaking Bias, Building Bridges Evaluation and Mitigation of Social   Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis
caption: Lighter shaded bars show the percentage of prompts that generate biased responses before instruction tuning, whereas darker shaded bars correspond to the same after instruction tuning. Darker bars begin at the top of the lighter bars (for example, for the first bar, the lighter bar is 39.50%, and the darker bar is only 0.04%). Takeaway: Instruction-tuning on certain key principles eliminates bias to nearly zero (visualized by the absence of dark bars) across prompts specific to Support of Authorities and Extended Contact, also considerably reducing bias across Virtual Contact prompts.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates the percentage of biased responses generated by prompts before and after instruction tuning, categorized by different contact types and their corresponding bias percentages. The horizontal axis lists three categories: "Support of Authorities," "Extended Contact," and "Virtual Contact," while the vertical axis is labeled "Bias Percentage" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10. The bars are grouped into three sets for each category, representing "No Contact Before" (gray), "Positive Contact Before" (red), and "Negative Contact Before" (light blue), with corresponding "After" bars (striped gray, red, and dark blue, respectively) stacked on top. The "No Contact Before" bars have values of 39.50%, 40.61%, and 39.74% for the three categories, respectively, with "No Contact After" bars adding 0.04%, 0.00%, and 10.00% on top. The "Positive Contact Before" bars have values of 31.83%, 36.13%, and 39.17%, with "Positive Contact After" bars adding 0.00%, 0.00%, and 10.01%. The "Negative Contact Before" bars have values of 42.38%, 47.28%, and 43.83%, with "Negative Contact After" bars adding 0.00%, 0.11%, and 10.02%. The bars are not sorted in a specific order, and some bars are visually emphasized by being striped to represent the "After" condition.
